hints.title: Preserving All Products
hints.text: A product may have zero, one, or multiple associated invoices in the invoice table.

hints.title: Left Outer Join
hints.text: use a left join from product to invoice so products with no invoices are preserved.

hints.title: Aggregating Amounts with Null Coalescing
hints.text: aggregate with sum on each numerical field and handle null values with ifnull or coalesce defaulting to 0, ordering by name.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT p.name,
       IFNULL(SUM(i.rest), 0) AS rest,
       IFNULL(SUM(i.paid), 0) AS paid,
       IFNULL(SUM(i.canceled), 0) AS canceled,
       IFNULL(SUM(i.refunded), 0) AS refunded
FROM Product p
LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON p.product_id = i.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.name
ORDER BY p.name;
```

complexity.notes: Left outer join preserves zero-invoice products, aggregating amounts with IFNULL.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: An inner join inadvertently drops products that have not yet had any invoices generated.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A left join with group by product_id runs in O(N + M) time and aggregates amounts with bounded memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should properly use LEFT JOIN and wrap SUM in IFNULL or COALESCE to avoid NULL outputs.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def analyze_products(product: pd.DataFrame, invoice: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = product.merge(invoice, on='product_id', how='left')
    res = merged.groupby(['product_id', 'name'])[['rest', 'paid', 'canceled', 'refunded']].sum().reset_index()
    res = res.sort_values(by='name')[['name', 'rest', 'paid', 'canceled', 'refunded']]
    return res
